name: University of Edinburgh, School of Informatics
why: PhD home institution with the Institute for Language, Cognition and Computation, the Autonomous Agents Research Group and a large XAI/responsible-AI community.

name: Centre for Technomoral Futures (Edinburgh Futures Institute)
why: Shannon Vallor's centre on AI ethics and technomoral futures, a natural fit for AI epistemic risk and public-facing safety work; posts are advertised on the Edinburgh jobs site.

name: University of Oxford, Department of Computer Science
why: Strong groups in human-centred computing, responsible AI and multi-agent systems (e.g. Michael Wooldridge).

name: Oxford Internet Institute
why: Social science of AI and the internet, with Sandra Wachter's and Brent Mittelstadt's governance-of-AI and explanation work closely matching XAI and AI-in-society interests.

name: University of Cambridge, Department of Computer Science and Technology
why: Home to Cambridge's ML, HCI and AI-safety-adjacent groups (e.g. David Krueger's former group), with regular assistant-professor calls.

name: Leverhulme Centre for the Future of Intelligence
why: Interdisciplinary AI centre whose Kinds of Intelligence and AI evaluation work (José Hernández-Orallo, Lucy Cheke) bridges cognitive science, AI safety and philosophy.

name: University of Cambridge, Department of History and Philosophy of Science
why: One of the world's leading HPS departments, right for philosophy-of-science and metascience work on AI; its posts appear in Cambridge's academic vacancies listing.

name: University College London (CS, STEaPP, Gatsby)
why: UCL hosts the Research on Research Institute (in STEaPP), the UCL AI Centre and the Gatsby Unit, which together cover metascience and ML.

name: Imperial College London
why: Strong in AI and multi-agent systems, including Francesca Toni's argumentation-based XAI group in Computing.

name: King's College London (Informatics and Digital Humanities)
why: Trustworthy autonomous systems, agents research and the Digital Humanities / Science & Technology Studies departments.

name: London School of Economics (Philosophy, Logic & Scientific Method)
why: LSE's philosophy-of-science department (CPNSS) and Data Science Institute suit work bridging metascience and AI.

name: University of Manchester
why: Large CS department with autonomous systems and human-centred AI groups, plus Manchester Institute of Innovation Research (science policy).

name: University of Bristol
why: Bristol Interactive AI CDT, Jean Golding Institute and a strong philosophy-of-science centre (Centre for Science and Philosophy).

name: The Alan Turing Institute
why: UK national institute for data science and AI, with public-policy, AI-ethics and research-integrity programmes.

name: Ada Lovelace Institute
why: Independent research institute on AI and society, whose research roles suit work on public-facing AI safety and epistemic risks.

name: UK AI Security Institute
why: Government AI safety institute hiring research scientists in evaluations, societal resilience and science of evals.

name: ETH Zurich, Department of Computer Science
why: Assistant professorships and fellowships in CS, including the Institute for Machine Learning and the SPY Lab (AI security).

name: ETH AI Center
why: Interdisciplinary AI hub with a postdoc fellowship scheme open to AI-and-society topics.

name: University of Zurich
why: Digital Society Initiative and Center for Reproducible Science (Leonhard Held), directly relevant to metascience.

name: EPFL
why: Top CS school with the Center for Intelligent Systems, the Data Science Lab (Robert West) and computational social science.

name: TU Munich, School of Computation, Information and Technology
why: Large tenure-track system, plus the TUM Think Tank and the Institute for Ethics in AI.

name: LMU Munich (job portal)
why: Covers the Munich Center for Machine Learning and the philosophy faculty.

name: Munich Center for Mathematical Philosophy (LMU)
why: A leading centre for formal philosophy of science and epistemology (Hannes Leitgeb, Stephan Hartmann), well suited to philosophy-of-science work on AI; posts are on the LMU job portal.

name: Saarland University / Saarland Informatics Campus
why: A major CS hub including the Center for Perspicuous Computing (explainability) and the Explainable Intelligent Systems philosophy–CS collaboration.

name: University of Tübingen
why: The Cluster of Excellence 'Machine Learning for Science' and its philosophy of ML group ask how ML changes scientific practice, the core of metascience-of-AI.

name: Tübingen AI Center
why: Recruits independent group leaders and professors across ML, with strong ties to the ML-for-science cluster.

name: ELLIS Institute Tübingen
why: Hires principal investigators on generous, independent terms; its groups include AI safety and alignment.

name: Max Planck Institute for Intelligent Systems
why: Includes the Social Foundations of Computation department (Moritz Hardt) on ML's scientific and societal foundations.

name: Max Planck Institute for Software Systems
why: Tenure-track faculty hiring, with groups on human-AI interaction and multi-agent learning (Goran Radanović, Manuel Gomez-Rodriguez).

name: Max Planck Institute for Human Development
why: Center for Humans and Machines (Iyad Rahwan) and Adaptive Rationality groups, spanning cognitive science and AI's social impact.

name: CISPA Helmholtz Center for Information Security
why: Well-funded tenure-track faculty hiring, including trustworthy and secure AI.

name: BIH QUEST Center for Responsible Research
why: Leading metascience and research-integrity centre (founded by Ulrich Dirnagl) on reproducibility and research quality; jobs are on the BIH career portal.

name: Hertie School, Centre for Digital Governance
why: Research centre on AI governance and digital policy with postdoc and faculty openings.

name: TU Delft
why: The Delft Digital Ethics Centre and the Interactive Intelligence group are strong on value-sensitive design, hybrid intelligence and XAI.

name: University of Amsterdam
why: Home to the Amsterdam Machine Learning Lab, ILLC (logic and philosophy) and the Institute for Advanced Study.

name: Utrecht University
why: Strong in multi-agent systems and argumentation, and host of the Descartes Centre for the history and philosophy of science.

name: Radboud University
why: The Donders Institute and the AI department (Iris van Rooij's critical cognitive science of AI) fit cognitive science and AI epistemics.

name: Leiden University / CWTS
why: CWTS (Centre for Science and Technology Studies) is a world leader in science studies and research evaluation, core territory for metascience of AI.

name: Tilburg University / Meta-Research Center
why: Jelte Wicherts' Meta-Research Center studies research integrity, questionable research practices and fraud.

name: KTH Royal Institute of Technology
why: WASP-funded AI hiring, with the Division of Robotics, Perception and Learning and a human-centred technology group.

name: Chalmers University of Technology
why: WASP and WASP-HS positions in AI and humanities/society, plus the Chalmers AI Research Centre.

name: Aalto University
why: FCAI (Finnish Center for AI), with strong human-AI interaction and computational cognitive modelling (Antti Oulasvirta).

name: University of Helsinki
why: FCAI partner with Philosophy and the Centre for Philosophy of Social Science (TINT), which has a strong philosophy of science tradition.

name: University of Copenhagen
why: The Pioneer Centre for AI, DIKU's NLP/XAI groups and a strong philosophy of science section.

name: Technical University of Denmark (DTU)
why: DTU Compute's cognitive systems and AI sections, part of the Pioneer Centre for AI.

name: Inria
why: France's national CS institute, with permanent researcher competitions (CRCN/ISFP) and teams on XAI and multi-agent systems.

name: Institute of Science and Technology Austria (ISTA)
why: Tenure-track assistant professorships in CS and ML (e.g. Christoph Lampert), with a highly interdisciplinary campus.

name: Complexity Science Hub
why: Its science-of-science and computational social science groups match metascience and complex social dynamics, continuing the CMU ICSD line of work.

name: ELLIS (European Laboratory for Learning and Intelligent Systems)
why: Pan-European ML network whose units and job board list PI, postdoc and faculty positions.

name: European AI Office (European Commission)
why: Implements the EU AI Act, and hires technology specialists and AI evaluators for general-purpose AI safety.

name: OECD (AI Policy Observatory / Directorate for STI)
why: The OECD.AI and Science, Technology and Innovation directorates work on AI policy and on AI in science.

name: Google DeepMind
why: Research scientist roles in the Responsibility, AGI Safety, Science and socio-technical research teams.

name: Anthropic
why: London research office; its interpretability, alignment and societal impacts teams study how AI affects people and science.

name: OpenAI
why: London research office, with openings such as research scientist roles on AI's cognitive and learning outcomes.

name: Microsoft Research Cambridge
why: Industry lab with a strong publication culture; its Sociotechnical Alignment and human-AI experience groups fit directly.

name: Meta FAIR
why: FAIR research scientist roles in Paris and London, covering fundamental and responsible AI.

name: Apple Machine Learning Research
why: Apple's ML research teams in Europe, with growing interest in reasoning, evaluation and publishing.

name: Mistral AI
why: Europe's leading frontier-model lab, with research roles in Paris and London.

name: Sony AI
why: Research team with an AI ethics flagship and a Zurich office.

name: Amazon Science
why: Applied scientist roles in European offices, including Tübingen causality and Cambridge AGI teams.

name: Spotify Research
why: Research on algorithmic responsibility, human-centred recommender systems and user modelling.

name: Bloomberg AI Engineering
why: A large NLP/AI research group that publishes actively, with a London hub.

name: Huawei Zurich Research Center
why: Part of Huawei's European Research Institute, hiring AI researchers in Zurich.

name: NAVER LABS Europe
why: A publication-oriented industrial lab in ML, NLP, robotics and human-robot interaction.

name: Cohere
why: Cohere Labs (formerly Cohere For AI) runs open-science research from London and elsewhere.

name: Hugging Face
why: Open-science ML company with research roles on evaluation, ethics and society (e.g. Margaret Mitchell's team).

name: Apollo Research
why: London AI safety organisation focused on evaluations of deception and scheming in frontier models.

name: FAR.AI
why: AI safety research nonprofit that hires remote research scientists and runs alignment workshops.

name: Epoch AI
why: Research on AI trends, compute and forecasting, much of it quantitative metascience of AI progress.

name: Centre for the Governance of AI (GovAI)
why: AI governance research institute with research fellow and scholar roles.
